thread:
maya: quick sync — we need to pick shipping approach for the internal API canary tomorrow. two options: thin HTTP shim that transcodes JSON<->proto at the edge, or a gRPC-native router. decision affects telemetry, quotas, and rollout UX. any last thoughts?

liam: shim = fastest to roll out for teams. fewer code changes in services. downside: harder to get faithful gRPC trace context and per-rpc metrics.

sam: +1 on gRPC router for fidelity. we get end-to-end latency, proper status codes, streaming semantics preserved. implementation effort is higher but reduces our oscilloscope later.

nora: what's the telemetry delta? how many extra metrics would shim need to approximate gRPC signals? we should quantify cost.

kevin: rough sketch: shim needs extra metrics: transcode_latency_ms, request_size_bytes, proto_version_header, model-routing-weight. also need a way to mark sampled full-proto payloads for debugging.

maya: can we do a hybrid? start with shim for public routes but route internal service-to-service via gRPC when the client supports it. rollout flag per-route in console.

sam: hybrid seems reasonable. but we must ensure header claim propagation is consistent (tenant-id, auth-level, trace). shim has to forward x-rw-tenant and preserve x-trace-id.

liam: agreed. also recommend a sampling policy to limit telemetry egress: default 1% full payload, 100% headers+status, 100% error traces. configurable per-tenant.

nora: can the console show per-route sampling and effective telemetry cost estimate before enabling? that's important for PMs.

kevin: yes — we can expose a UI panel: Sampling % -> estimated events/day -> estimated GB/day -> projected ingestion cost. backend proto: \n\n```\nroute_policy:\n  path: /api/v1/generate\n  routing: hybrid\n  weights:\n    grpc: 70\n    shim: 30\n  sampling:\n    full_payload_pct: 1\n    headers_only_pct: 100\n    error_capture: true\n```\n
maya: nice. that config should be part of the rollout plan. for canary tomorrow let's do: grpc:0 shim:100 for external callers, internal clients 0/100 -> ramp by weight map over 24h. start sampling 1% full payload.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: service-internal-router v2 at 2026-03-21T10:00:00Z — weight map applied for route /api/v1/generate : {grpc:0, shim:100} — :rocket:

sam: one more ask — add console graph for transcode_latency_ms with p50/p95/p99 by routing path (shim vs grpc). we should surface regression alerts if p95_shim - p95_grpc > 50ms.

liam: will add telemetry dashboard card + an alert rule: condition p95_delta > 50ms sustained 5m -> pager to eng-platform.

nora: and quota enforcement? shim needs to respect tenant quota counters exactly like gRPC path. otherwise cost accounting breaks.

kevin: implement a shared quota service hook that both shim and grpc-router call (token exchange). keep idempotency key on proxied requests.

maya: ok action items: liam add dashboard + alert, kevin wire quota hook + sampling flags, sam validate gRPC router perf tests, nora produce telemetry cost estimate for PMs, i'll draft rollout steps in the console playbook. final check-in in #eng-platform at 09:30 UTC tomorrow. :eyes:

kevin: ack. I'll post a small perf log after local run.

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded: 2026-03-21T10:02:15Z — health checks OK — current weights: {grpc:0, shim:100}

maya: thanks team — we'll monitor. if any regression, rollback to previous routing immediately.

liam: will watch the p95 charts and post updates. :thumbsup:
